content:
I'd like to work on bordism / cobordism here, and would appreciate a pointer on the right entry point, because the chain down to something available looks blocked and I'd rather ask than guess.

What I worked out. Bordism lives in GeometricTopology layer 6 ("knot concordance and 4D cobordism"), whose target is the cobordism category with "composition by gluing (layer 1)". Layer 1's gluing is not on main and I don't see it in an open PR. The roadmap says collars are what make a gluing smooth, and the collar target is itself blocked on the inverse function theorem for manifolds — a Mathlib TODO I wrote up in this topic. So:

layer 6 cobordism category
  -> layer 1 gluing            (absent)
    -> collars                 (absent)
      -> global collar theorem (blocked)
        -> manifold IFT        (Mathlib TODO)

Where I've been useful so far. I contributed the collar-chart end: #3104 (collar charts on an arbitrary manifold with boundary) and #3358 (those charts are C^k diffeomorphisms between source and target), both merged. Boundary-as-a-manifold is on main in Boundary/Charts. What is missing between there and gluing is the global collar theorem, not the local theory.

For context on the wider landscape: Mathlib's own Mathlib/Geometry/Manifold/Bordism.lean has SingularManifold and a TODO list for everything after it (the bordism relation, the group, the ring, relative groups), and it has had no mathematical content added since May 2025 — blocked on the same collar and gluing theorems.

My question: where would you point someone who wants to work on bordism? Options I can see, and I don't know which is wanted:

  1. Contribute the manifold IFT — a Mathlib PR rather than one here — to unblock collars, then gluing, then cobordism. This looks like the real bottleneck and I am happy to take it on if that is the consensus.
  2. Define cobordisms and prove the parts of the relation that need no gluing (reflexivity, symmetry), leaving composition and transitivity until gluing lands. I am unsure whether scope.md's "material built for a later stage while its stated prerequisite stage is absent" would rule this out.
  3. Something else — e.g. a topological gluing first, if that is a useful intermediate, or a layer-1 item I have not spotted.

Happy to be told the answer is "not yet, work on something else"; I would just rather hear it than open a PR that gets turned away on scope.

Note that I have done (2) in a mathlib PR --- which was (for a long time) blocked on the proper definition of smooth embeddings (which mathlib now has, docs#Manifold.IsSmoothEmbedding), and now is blocked on me finishing my higher-priority tasks (such as applications and paper writing).

Mod note: I've deleted a comment that (by all looks of it) is AI-written response here (but left the initial post, even though it shows the same signs). Everybody is welcome to comment, please do so using your own words.
